headline: Approved $1,658,901.00 FY28 library budget and up to $3,500 for two staff computers.
summary: Trustees accepted Trustee Mallick's resignation and voted to post the open trustee seat through November 30. Staff will join the director candidate interviews on November 5 and 6. A book donation policy will be voted on at the next meeting.

plain_text:
Leach Library Board of Trustees
Draft Meeting minutes
November 4, 2026 at 7:00 PM
Leach Library, Londonderry NH
Members Present:
 Nancy Hendricks, Chair
 Beth Marrocco, Vice-Chair
 Erica Laue, Secretary
 Azra Palo, Treasurer
 Moira Ryan, Trustee
 Donna Plante, Interim Library Director
Members Absent:
 Jan McLaughlin, Trustee
Call to Order: made by Chair Hendricks at 7 PM.
Consent Agenda:
 October 7, 2026 minutes
 Next meetings: 12/2, 1/6/27
 Motion to accept the consent agenda made by Secretary Laue, seconded by 
Treasurer Palo. Motion passes 5-1.
Public Comment: None.
Staff Reports: presented by Interim Director Plante
 ENE has determined that some of our temperature issues stem from a wiring issue that 
predates ENE’s services. They estimate it will take two technicians approximately one 
week to do the work, for approximately $8,000. We will likely have to defer this until the 
next FY.
 The loose handrail outside the building has been epoxied- thank you Bob Slater!
 The glycol installation is scheduled for next week, to be paid under the Phase IIA 
purchase order.
 1,778 reference questions were answered in September.
 45 people attended the presentation on the Mount Washington Observatory.
 Right now the display upstairs is on Native American Heritage Month. We will also have 
displays for Veteran’s Day next week.
 We will have our first-ever wrapping paper swap on 11/21.
 We are partnering with the Currier Museum for a Tomi DePaola craft in December.
 In September, we had 4,950 new visitors to the library, and 150+ new cardholders 
registered!
 Teens are spending more time at the library, both for our programs and to do their 
homework etc.
 Interim Director Plante was interviewed by the Access Center for an upcoming program.
 Staff are getting a lot of positive feedback about the new fine-free policy, and Becca has 
been invited to write a weekly column in the Derry News. Nick got to represent Leach at 
a conference in Burlington, VT.
 Winter Reading will start in January and run through mid-February.
Treasurer’s Report: presented by Treasurer Palo
 Book account: $49,852.13 as of the end of September.
 Trustee account: $43,973.43 as of the end of September.
 Library budget for FY28 will be workshopped at the Town Council meeting on 11/16 at 6 
PM and 11/17 at 6:30 at the budget committee meeting.
 We hope to get the financial ad hoc committee back together after the new director has 
been hired, to address the designations on the funds in the Trustee account.
Committee Reports:
 Director search, presented by Secretary Laue: Four top candidates have been identified 
and offered interviews. Three of them have accepted interviews and will be interviewed 
on 11/5 and 11/6. 
 Motion to include staff in the director interviews made by Secretary Laue, 
seconded by Treasurer Palo. Discussion on what that will entail and whether all 
Trustees will have access to the candidates’ resumes. Motion passes 5-0.
Presentations and Discussion:
 Meetings: presented by Chair Hendricks. Having to cancel meetings due to a lack of 
quorum, particularly when individuals are not communicating their absences in advance, 
is unacceptable. We have a remote participation policy and the ability to communicate 
the need for such accommodations.
o Trustee Ryan objects to feeling picked on. Other members of the Board 
emphasize the importance of the communication aspect.
 Process for Library Director Search: Discussed under the search committee item.
 Open Position Updates: The part-time children’s librarian position is open until 11/6, and 
then management staff will review resumes and identify candidates to interview.
 Building Update: Discussed under staff reports. Chair Hendricks notes that she was 
contacted by Bob Slater to discuss updates for the coming year.
 Process for Appointing New Trustee: Chair Hendricks states that Kirsten has affirmed 
that we need to advertise the open position once, in one newspaper, in order to be legal.
She suggests keeping the position open for a couple of weeks before we follow the 
process that was set out in the Bylaws to recommend a candidate for appointment. Chair
Hendricks suggests having the ad put in the Londonderry Times on 11/12 and have the 
position open through 11/30. Motion by Secretary Laue to post the position and keep
it open through the 30th, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Clarification on sourcing 
the payment from the Trustee account. Motion passes 4-1.
o Motion to pay for the posting from the Trustee account, to spend no more 
than $125, made by Treasurer Palo, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. 
Motion passes 4-1.
 Book Sale Donations Policy: Interim Director Plante states that there have been 
guidelines in the past for managing donations, but no formal policies that permit staff to 
turn away donations when the library is at capacity or the items are too damaged to 
utilize. Interim Director Plante has drafted a policy based on the currently-existing
guidelines, with limitations set on the number of donations that a person can make in a 
day and the condition of the materials. We will vote on this policy at our next meeting.
Deliberations and Vote:
 Acceptance of Trustee Resignation: Trustee Mallick has submitted her resignation, citing
scheduling conflicts. Motion to accept her resignation made by Secretary Laue, 
seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion passes 5-0.
 FY28 Department Budget: Interim Director Plante notes that our budget presentation 
slides are complete and will be submitted to the Board before the public sees them. 
Finance had to make some adjustments to our final numbers based on the correct 
numbers for disability and liability insurances etc., so the new overall total for the FY28 
budget is decreased by $1,774.00, making the new total $1,658,901.00. Motion by 
Secretary Laue, seconded by Treasurer Palo, to accept the FY28 budget total at 
$1,658,901.00. Motion passes 5-0.
 Records Retention Policy Draft: This is a preexisting policy with two changes requested. 
The Minor Records Request Form is under permanent retention, though the law does 
not specify what retention should look like. Motion by Vice Chair Marrocco to accept 
the retention policy with proposed changes, seconded by Secretary Laue. Motion 
passes 5-0.
 Friends of the Leach Library Proposals:
o Digital Display Birthday Fundraiser: This would allow patrons to make a donation 
in exchange for having a slide celebrating someone’s birthday up for a week. The
Friends will do the work of creating the slides, and the staff will put them in the 
rotation accordingly. Motion by Secretary Laue to accept this proposal, 
seconded by Treasurer Palo. Discussion regarding two-household families and 
confidentiality of children. Motion passes 4-1.
o Door Harp Raffle Fundraiser: This proposes to have a handmade door harp 
raffled off between 11/30 and 12/11, with the drawing to happen in advance of 
the Bell Ringer concert in December. The proposal is coming to the Trustees for 
transparency regarding having raffle sales at the circulation desk. Motion by 
Secretary Laue to accept this proposal, seconded by Treasurer Palo. 
Motion passes 5-0.
 Contracts:
o McIntire Business Products: $499.00 for services related to our laminator. This is 
usually paid from the maintenance line of the budget, but could be paid from the 
equipment budget line. Motion by Secretary Laue to pay $499.00 from the 
equipment line of the budget, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion 
passes 5-0.
o ENE Systems of New Hampshire Service Agreement: This begins 12/1 and is for 
$3,175.00, normally paid from the maintenance line of the budget. Trustee Ryan 
asks if we have considered using other contractors; Interim Director Plante notes 
that ENE serves the entire town campus and now the school district as well. It 
would also cost more to change providers at this time. Motion by Secretary 
Laue to pay $3,175.00 to ENE from the maintenance line of the budget, 
seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Discussion about whether two clauses are 
contradictory. Motion passes 4-0-1, with Trustee Ryan abstaining.
 Funding Requests: presented by Interim Director Plante.
o Wowbrary: This is a patron request. It generates social media posts and emails 
for the library that highlight new content and events for the public. Treasurer Palo
affirms that Rogers Memorial Library uses it, and it helps save staff time. The
GMILCS member rate would be $400, and they would prorate us for this year. 
Their board has also made it a policy never to increase their fees. Discussion 
revolves around which accounts and line items could be used to pay for the 
service, now and in June. Motion made by Secretary Laue to pay up to $300 
from the Trustee account for Wowbrary, seconded by Treasurer Palo. 
Motion passes 5-0.
o New desktop computers: We need at least one desktop staff computer, and the 
replaced computer would become a public computer. Brand new, as of mid-
September, the recommended computer would cost $1,536.26; refurbished 
models are approximately $1,200.00. While a laptop and docking setup is an 
option, that would not fit with our current computing uses and needs. Interim 
Director Plante requests two, noting that only one is strictly necessary, to be paid
out of the machinery line of the budget. This will overspend the line. Motion 
made by Secretary Laue to expend up to $3,500.00 from the machinery line 
of the budget for two computers, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion
passes 5-0.
o NH BET Training: This is an online training to support managers working in a 
union environment. The cost is $115.00 per attendee, with Interim Director Plante
attending, coming out of the seminars line of the budget. Motion made by 
Secretary Laue to expend $115.00 from the seminars line of the budget, 
seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Discussion about whether multiple staff can
attend. Motion passes 5-0.
o Financial Times subscription: This is a patron request for the Saturday edition of 
the Financial Times, costing $164.68 through our subscription service. 
Discussion revolves around the wisdom of adding a subscription back in when 
we just cut several, and whether asking the Friends to cover it is a viable option. 
Motion made by Secretary Laue to approve the expenditure of $164.68. No 
second made. Motion fails.
o 2027 Staff Summer Reading T-Shirts: This is a request from the staff for t-shirts 
to promote the summer reading program, for a total of $209.10. Motion made by
Secretary Laue to expend $209.10 from the Trustee account for staff t-
shirts, seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion passes 5-0.
o Swank Movie License: This allows Leach to show movies during programs. We 
used to pay for this with a group rate through the NH State Library; the State 
Library has cancelled their purchase, but Swank has agreed to license the 
program to us at the discounted rate of $409.00. Motion made by Vice Chair 
Marrocco to pay $409.00 for Swank out of the management services line of 
the budget, seconded by Secretary Laue. Motion passes 5-0.
 Acceptance of unanticipated funds under RSA 202-A:4-c:
o Anonymous donor: Seven $5 gift cards to Dunkin Donuts for staff appreciation.
o Purnima Srinivasan: $101.00 in unrestricted funding.
o Motion made by Secretary Laue to accept these unanticipated funds under 
RSA 202-A:4-c, seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion passes 5-0.
Public Comment:
 Linda Lampkin, 4 Griffin Road: Linda would like to highlight the Paranormal Night hosted
by Becca, and the Edgar Allen Poe reading event, which were both packed events at 
Leach. 
Adjournment: motion made by Secretary Laue at 8:45, unanimously agreed.
Minutes prepared by Secretary Laue.
